When the AI Gateway streams a response c.title: Tool history relies on ordered calls, grouped results, and signature round trips
answers: What ordering does tool-result conversion require?
How are parallel tool responses grouped?
How are tool IDs, arguments, and thought signatures translated?
When the AI Gateway streams a response c.body:
mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model builds an ID-to-function-name map while visiting assistant tool calls. A later tool message indexes that map using tool_call_id, so its matching call must already have appeared. Assistant messages with tool calls become model functionCall parts; that branch does not include the assistant's content. Arguments are parsed from JSON strings. A truthy thought_signature is emitted beside functionCall as thoughtSignature.
Consecutive tool results are combined into one user turn only when the previous turn is a nonempty user turn containing exclusively functionResponse parts. mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:_tool_result_to_response ensures each response is an object: JSON objects pass through, other decoded JSON values are wrapped under result, and content that cannot be decoded is wrapped unchanged.
mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice preserves mixed response text and calls, concatenating all text parts. It JSON-serializes arguments and preserves supplied call IDs; absent IDs become call_ plus an MD5 digest of the function name and serialized arguments. It reads camel-case or snake-case thought signatures at the part level before falling back to the functionCall object. Streaming calls contain full arguments and each ToolCallDelta receives index=0.

GeminiAdapter converts assistant tool calls to functionCall parts without assistant content, parses JSON arguments, and emits truthy thought_signature as thoughtSignature. Tool results preserve JSON objects and wrap other decoded values or undecodable content under result. Gemini-to-OpenAI conversion concatenates mixed text, JSON-serializes call arguments, preserves supplied IDs or generates call_ IDs using MD5, reads camel-case or snake-case signatures from parts before functionCall objects, and emits streaming ToolCallDelta entries with full arguments and index=0.

When the tracking server is under heavy.title: Application construction and native-route precedence
answers: Where is the ASGI application constructed?
Which routes take precedence over Flask?
How does the factory apply static prefixes?
Are generated API documentation endpoints enabled?
When the tracking server is under heavy.body: mlflow/server/fastapi_app.py:create_fastapi_app constructs the FastAPI application; the module invokes this factory to create the ASGI app instance. It reads the static prefix, strips trailing slashes, and rejects braces. OpenAPI, Swagger, and ReDoc endpoints are disabled. The factory initializes security, workspace middleware, and gateway timing, then includes native routers before mounting Flask at '/'. OTEL, jobs, gateway, and assistant routers receive the static prefix directly. The artifact router is included without a factory-supplied prefix; MCP router prefixes come from its prefix helper. MCP exception handlers are installed before the MCP router is included. Native routers must remain before the catch-all Flask mount to take precedence. The factory accepts an alternative Flask application.
When the tracking server is under heavy.applies: Adding native routers, changing application assembly, configuring URL prefixes, or wrapping a different Flask application.
When the tracking server is under heavy.searchInstances: FastAPI application construction in create_fastapi_app registers native routers before the catch-all Flask mount at '/' so native routes take precedence, normalizes the static prefix by stripping trailing slashes and rejecting braces, and accepts an alternative Flask application. OTEL, jobs, gateway, and assistant routers receive the static prefix directly; artifact_router receives no factory-supplied prefix, and MCP uses its prefix helper with exception handlers installed before router inclusion. The factory initializes security, workspace middleware, and gateway timing, disables OpenAPI, Swagger, and ReDoc endpoints, and is invoked by the module to create the ASGI app instance.

On a registered model that uses stages,.title: Alias lookup and stage transitions use distinct selection rules
answers: How does the reserved latest alias resolve?
What validation precedes alias assignment?
When does a stage transition archive other versions?
On a registered model that uses stages,.body:
mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.set_registered_model_alias validates the alias, including reserved-name restrictions, validates the version, resolves a nondeleted target version, and merges an alias row carrying that version's workspace.
mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.get_model_version_by_alias treats the case-insensitive latest alias specially: it returns the first result from get_latest_versions, or raises RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST if none exists. Other aliases require the registered model to exist, resolve an alias row and then a nondeleted version, and raise INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE when the alias is missing.
mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.get_latest_versions takes latest_versions from the registered-model entity, filters by canonical stages, and attaches matching aliases. None or empty stages means all stages.
mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.transition_model_version_stage allows archive_existing_versions only for active destination stages. In one write session it archives other versions of the same model in that canonical stage, updates their timestamps, changes the target stage, and updates the target and parent timestamps. It returns the target with aliases populated.

When I stream a response through the AI.title: Anthropic streaming separates event accumulation from delta conversion
answers: Where are stream metadata and token usage accumulated?
Which Anthropic events produce gateway chunks?
How do content-block indices and streamed tool-call indices map?
When I stream a response through the AI.body:
mlflow/gateway/providers/anthropic.py:AnthropicProvider._chat_stream encodes and adapts the request, applies the payload hook, and opens the stream. It strips incoming chunks, ignores empty chunks and non-data lines, and JSON-decodes data lines. message_start supplies the id, model, input-token count, and cache-token counts; this event is consumed without yielding a chat response.
Only message_delta, content_block_start, and content_block_delta proceed to conversion. The provider remembers each distinct non-null content-block index and injects the saved id and model into subsequent events. On message_delta it updates output tokens, attaches accumulated usage under _usage_data, and emits one converted response for each remembered index. Content-block events are converted directly.
mlflow/gateway/providers/anthropic.py:AnthropicAdapter.model_to_chat_streaming selects delta, then content_block, then an empty dictionary as its content source. tool_use starts a function tool call with id and name; input_json_delta carries partial_json as function arguments. Both use tool-call index 0, while the enclosing choice uses the event's index. Other content supplies a text delta. A present stop reason maps max_tokens to length and other values to stop. Usage is built only when _usage_data is present and truthy.
When I stream a response through the AI.applies: Changing Anthropic streaming events, metadata propagation, tool-call deltas, finish reasons, or usage emission.
When I stream a response through the AI.searchInstances: Anthropic streaming separates event accumulation in AnthropicProvider from delta conversion in AnthropicAdapter: message_start saves metadata and token counts without yielding, content-block events convert directly, and message_delta emits a response for each remembered content-block index with accumulated usage. Covers message_start, message_delta, content_block_start, content_block_delta, id, model, input tokens, output tokens, cache tokens, and _usage_data. Conversion prefers delta over content_block; tool_use supplies function-call id and name, input_json_delta supplies partial_json arguments, tool-call index is 0, and choice index follows the event. Other content produces text deltas, max_tokens maps to length, other present stop reasons map to stop, and usage requires truthy _usage_data.

Copying or serializing trace data fails.title: LazySpan keeps dictionary export separate from one-time materialization
answers: When does LazySpan construct its OTel-backed state?
When may export reuse the original stored JSON?
Why must to_dict invalidate raw JSON even without an observed mutation?
Copying or serializing trace data fails.body:
mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan.__init__ deliberately skips the base initializer and retains the supplied dictionary, optional raw JSON, and a materialization flag. mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan.from_stored_content parses stored JSON and applies load-time translation; it retains the original JSON only when translation reports no modification.
mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan.to_dict returns the actual mutable stored dictionary and clears raw JSON immediately. Preserve that invalidation: once callers can mutate the dictionary, the original JSON cannot safely represent subsequent exports. mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan.json_for_export returns retained raw JSON when available, otherwise compactly serializes the stored dictionary.
mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan._ensure_materialized constructs a Span from the dictionary once and adopts its OTel span, attribute registry, attachments, and links. mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan.__getattr__ triggers this path for missing attributes and retries lookup. Materialization does not replace the dictionary used by export. mlflow/entities/span.py:LazySpan.__repr__ can display identifying fields without materialization and attempts to decode a JSON-encoded request ID.

This covers LazySpan.from_stored_content load-time translation and original JSON retention, to_dict mutation, and json_for_export raw JSON reuse or compact serialization. It also covers _ensure_materialized and __getattr__ adopting the Span’s OTel span, attribute registry, attachments, and links once, plus __repr__ displaying identifying fields and decoding a JSON-encoded request ID without materialization.

Endpoints in the AI Gateway that use the.title: Add provider-specific authentication through the mode configuration
answers: Where should a new provider authentication mode be added?
Are generic API-key fields inherited by custom modes?
Which shared builders interpret the mode and field configuration?
Endpoints in the AI Gateway that use the.body:
To add a provider-specific authentication mode, work in mlflow/utils/providers.py. First add or extend the provider's _PROVIDER_AUTH_MODES entry consumed by mlflow/utils/providers.py:get_provider_config_response. Use the provider key reached after that function's normalization and Bedrock alias handling. Define each mode's display_name, description, and fields; mark the intended default mode with default=true.
Next define each field's name, description, secret classification, required flag, and optional default. mlflow/utils/providers.py:_build_auth_mode_response performs the secret/config split, and mlflow/utils/providers.py:_build_response_field supplies response defaults and fixes the field type to string. Existing field properties need no builder changes.
A provider-specific entry replaces the generic fallback completely. Include api_key or api_base explicitly if the custom mode needs them; fields from mlflow/utils/providers.py:_build_simple_api_key_mode are not merged into configured modes. Keep the provider's mode collection nonempty because default selection falls back to its first response mode. For a change to the generic authentication form across fallback providers, edit _build_simple_api_key_mode instead.
Endpoints in the AI Gateway that use the.applies: Adding authentication modes or credential fields, configuring provider-specific defaults, or changing the generic API-key form.
Endpoints in the AI Gateway that use the.searchInstances: Provider-specific authentication is configured in _PROVIDER_AUTH_MODES using the normalized provider key after Bedrock alias handling; custom modes completely replace the generic authentication fallback. Modes define display_name, description, fields, and default=true, while fields define name, description, secret, required, and optional default; response builders separate secret and config fields and fix field types to string. Include api_key and api_base explicitly when needed because configured modes do not inherit them, and keep mode collections nonempty for default selection. Change _build_simple_api_key_mode for generic authentication forms across fallback providers.

When I send a chat request to a Gemini o.title: Generation requests share adapters across buffered and streaming routes
answers: Where do chat and completion requests enter the Gemini implementation?

When I send a chat request to a Gemini o.body:
mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiProvider._chat and mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiProvider._completions encode requests with exclude_none=True, check the model field, adapt the payload, send it to the configured model's generateContent endpoint, and adapt the response. mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiProvider._request supplies the configured provider headers and base URL.
mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiAdapter.completions_to_model turns prompt into a user message, optionally prepends system_prompt, and delegates to mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model. That shared adapter rejects mapped Gemini-native parameter names with HTTP 422, aliases max_completion_tokens only when max_tokens is absent, renames generation parameters, and selects supported generation settings. It collects system messages into system_instruction, translates JSON response formats into generationConfig, and accepts only function tools, using parametersJsonSchema for their parameter definitions.
mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiProvider._chat_stream and mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiProvider._completions_stream use the same request adapters but call streamGenerateContent?alt=sse. Both reassemble incomplete chunks, decode and strip them, ignore records without a data: prefix, stop at [DONE], parse JSON, and yield their respective streaming response adapters.
